lab: tools/mix_lab.py in a privileged container: 10 clients (own namespaces, kpclientd + http-proxy-client each) send HEAD requests at Poisson times (mean 30 s) to 30 live public websites (3 per client); phase 1 through a Katzenpost mixnet (3 voting authorities, 3 mix layers, 1 gateway, 1 service node with the HTTP proxy), phase 2 the same workload through a plain low-latency proxy (no mixing, no cover), as a multi-hop VPN's shared exit carries it
adversary: global passive: every client's link (send times only) and the service's internet link (each site's DNS lookup time); given the delay distribution (empirical from ground truth, and the network's own law: 5 Poisson hops at Mu); tools/gpa.py scores every client per request
notes: Mix-lane accuracy below chance is sampling noise: 298 requests, 95% interval about +/-3 points around 10%.
The baseline attacker uses the same capture, grouping and scoring code, and identifies 86% of senders: the attack works where timing leaks.
Busy and idle send rates on the mix lane are equal (real-or-drop and loop cover); on the baseline a client's link is silent until it sends.
Failed live fetches: 502 (the reply exceeds one 8000-byte mixnet message, or the site refused) and 504 (no reply within 60 s).
